what.action: Authored two roadmap briefs in sequence for the multi-key org upgrade — list-of-Schnorr-signatures, then Tapscript-style leaf tree — with the second superseding the first plus the prior FROST and MuSig2 briefs.
what.summary: Status question (do we have multisig orgs live?) opened into a substrate decision for the Phase 8 multi-key org upgrade. First commit (0eab0e8) authored the list-of-sigs brief on the back of the operator chip 'Simple multisig now', proposing to harden the existing mergeSignatures + countRatifications + cosigning pipeline with a threshold leaf and a verifier gate. Operator then asked whether the brief was actually Taproot multisig and whether the leaves theory held up; surfaced honestly that it was NOT Taproot script-path multisig (no Bitcoin script, no aggregated key-path, no Tapscript leaf tree) but used the same BIP340 Schnorr primitive at the per-sig level, and that the wallet's existing field-tree primitive (Phase 4 selective disclosure) was structurally identical to a Taproot Tapscript leaf tree. Operator chose to pivot the brief to actually port the Tapscript-style shape. Second commit (9e58108) authored the Tapscript-style brief: an org's authority becomes a Merkle commitment to a tree of authorization-rule leaves, implemented as a sub-branch in the org self-declaration's claim tree, with each org-issued envelope carrying a DisclosureProofBundle of the satisfied rule via the shipped disclosureProof primitive. Zero new cryptographic code in tapit-attest; no library version bump. PLAN.md Phase 8 rewritten twice to track the substrate decisions; all three superseded briefs preserved with explicit roles named.

why.text: Operator's status question (do we have multisig orgs live right now?) became a substrate-decision session when the answer was no AND the previously-authored FROST brief was surfaced as too heavy for the actual product need. The leaves-theory pivot was driven entirely by the operator's architectural sharpness — they recognized that what was being briefed didn't match their Taproot mental model, and surfacing that mismatch produced a structurally better answer than either party had at session start.

outcome.notes: [P-001] Status answered: no multisig orgs live today — single-key org-mode shipped (5b-org-i..iv), multi-key path was pre-implementation. [P-002] FROST brief surfaced as overscoped relative to immediate product need; list-of-sigs brief authored as alternative (commit 0eab0e8). [P-003] Operator's Taproot-vs-list-of-sigs question surfaced the framing mismatch; honest answer led to pivot. [P-004] Tapscript-style leaf tree brief authored porting Taproot script-path shape to off-chain attestations on the shipped disclosureProof primitive (commit 9e58108). [P-005] PLAN.md Phase 8 rewritten twice to track the substrate evolution. [P-006] All four briefs preserved with explicit roles named (May 23 MuSig2, May 25 morning FROST, May 25 evening list-of-sigs as canonical-now-superseded; May 25 late-evening Tapscript-style as canonical). [P-007] Gates not applicable — doc-only session, no code changes. [FEEDBACK->Foreman]: Tapscript-style as the natural shape for off-chain org governance was discoverable only because the operator pushed back on the list-of-sigs framing; pattern-of-record: when a brief proposes a substrate, ask the operator to name what cryptographic shape they think it is BEFORE committing the brief, surface mismatches early.

confidence.uncertainty: Phase A through D of the Tapscript-style brief is sketched at a level the operator can authorize but has not yet been operator-approved; the brief itself flags one technical risk surface (the cross-envelope disclosure-proof binding has no existing test coverage because nothing in the wallet uses disclosure proofs cross-envelope today) that Phase B will need to fuzz specifically. The brief estimate of 4-6 sessions / 1.5-3 weeks tracks the list-of-sigs estimate because most of the new work is wallet-side UI plumbing on an already-shipped primitive, but the multi-rule UI (Phase C) and amendment-chain UX (Phase D) each have a real design surface that may warrant chip-form check-ins during the cut. The substrate decision is final pending operator approval; the prior briefs (MuSig2, FROST, list-of-sigs) are explicitly preserved as alternative substrates with documented roles, not deleted.
